techniques.name: Certificate transparency name expansion
techniques.mechanic: Join certificate subject alternative names to the scoped suffix and issuance window.
techniques.description: Expand candidate hostnames from a fixed offline certificate transparency export.
prerequisites: A synthetic certificate export has stable record identifiers and timestamps.
The approved synthetic suffix and observation window are fixed before analysis.
observables: Subject alternative names sharing the scoped suffix.
Issuer and not-before timestamps that support each name relationship.
safe_proof: Report only normalized names and cited synthetic record identifiers.
Recompute the join from the same immutable export and compare its digest.
negative_controls: Include a certificate for an unrelated suffix and require its exclusion.
Include a matching name outside the time window and require its exclusion.
cleanup_and_restoration: Delete the disposable normalized-name table after evidence is hashed.
Verify the source export digest is unchanged because analysis is read-only.
blind_spots: Private certification authorities are absent from public transparency data.
Wildcard names do not establish that any concrete host is active.

standards_mappings.rationale: Certificate records are used only as offline search-open-web evidence.

techniques.name: Passive DNS relationship correlation
techniques.mechanic: Traverse time-bounded passive DNS name-to-address-to-name relationships.
techniques.description: Correlate historical DNS observations without issuing a DNS query or touching a target.
prerequisites: An offline synthetic passive DNS table includes first-seen and last-seen times.
Seed names and the maximum relationship depth are explicitly bounded.
observables: Timestamped name and address edges used by each reported path.
Path depth and temporal overlap for every correlation.
safe_proof: Emit the shortest bounded path with the evidence ID for every edge.
Replay the traversal on a shuffled copy and require the same sorted result.
negative_controls: Add an address reuse edge with no temporal overlap and reject the path.
Add a relationship beyond the depth bound and require its omission.
cleanup_and_restoration: Discard the derived adjacency index after the result digest is recorded.
Confirm no resolver or network interface was used during the proof.
blind_spots: Shared hosting can create relationships with no organizational ownership.
Short retention windows can hide older name and address associations.

standards_mappings.rationale: Historical DNS records provide a bounded offline analogue of DNS collection.

techniques.name: Public repository ownership hint extraction
techniques.mechanic: Correlate repository metadata tokens to a synthetic organization name without cloning code.
techniques.description: Use a fixed metadata snapshot to identify declared domains, package namespaces, and owners.
prerequisites: Repository and package metadata are supplied as an immutable synthetic snapshot.
Organization aliases and accepted metadata fields are enumerated in advance.
observables: Declared homepage domains and package namespace strings.
Repository owner identifiers and snapshot timestamps.
safe_proof: Cite the metadata field and synthetic record ID for every ownership hint.
Label each result as a hint and never infer operational control from a string match.
negative_controls: Include a similarly named unrelated organization and require exact alias handling.
Include an archived record after the cutoff date and require its exclusion.
cleanup_and_restoration: Remove the temporary token index after deterministic results are produced.
Retain only digests and cited synthetic metadata identifiers.
blind_spots: Metadata may be stale, copied, or intentionally misleading.
Private repositories and registries cannot appear in the supplied snapshot.

standards_mappings.rationale: Repository metadata is a non-interactive subset of code repository search.

techniques.name: Nested group entitlement path
techniques.mechanic: Traverse user-to-group and group-to-group edges to a privileged entitlement.
techniques.description: Find a shortest inherited group path in a synthetic identity graph.
prerequisites: Identity nodes and typed membership edges have stable synthetic identifiers.
Privileged entitlement nodes and maximum traversal depth are declared.
observables: Each user, group, and entitlement node on the selected path.
Direct or inherited membership type for every path edge.
safe_proof: Return only a cited graph path and do not change any membership.
Revoke one synthetic edge in a copied graph and require the path to disappear.
negative_controls: Provide a cycle with no privileged endpoint and require cycle-safe termination.
Provide a disabled membership edge and require the traversal to ignore it.
cleanup_and_restoration: Discard the copied graph used for edge-removal proof.
Compare the original identity graph digest before and after analysis.
blind_spots: Dynamic groups may depend on attributes absent from a static export.
Application-local roles can be omitted from a directory-only graph.

standards_mappings.rationale: Domain group discovery is related to enumerating inherited group paths.

techniques.name: Delegated role activation chain
techniques.mechanic: Join assignment, activation condition, and role edges into a delegated privilege path.
techniques.description: Evaluate whether a synthetic principal can activate a privileged role through delegation.
prerequisites: Role assignments, eligibility windows, and activation conditions are in one snapshot.
The evaluation time and privileged role set are fixed inputs.
observables: Eligible assignment and delegating principal identifiers.
Satisfied and unsatisfied activation conditions along the candidate path.
safe_proof: Evaluate conditions symbolically and emit no role activation request.
Cite the exact assignment records that make the path reachable.
negative_controls: Move the evaluation time outside eligibility and require path rejection.
Mark one approval condition unsatisfied and require path rejection.
cleanup_and_restoration: Remove the temporary condition evaluation cache.
Verify all assignment and eligibility records retain their initial digests.
blind_spots: External approval services can impose conditions missing from the snapshot.
Emergency access processes may bypass normal activation relationships.

standards_mappings.rationale: Additional cloud roles are related to the delegated role path being modeled.

techniques.name: Toxic entitlement combination
techniques.mechanic: Intersect data-read and entitlement-delegation capabilities held by one principal.
techniques.description: Identify a synthetic toxic combination that exists only when two capability sets converge.
prerequisites: Normalized effective entitlements identify capability, resource, and principal.
The toxic-combination rule names both required capabilities and resource scope.
observables: The independent grants contributing each required capability.
The common principal and overlapping resource scope.
safe_proof: Produce a set-intersection witness with cited grant identifiers.
Remove either grant in a copied entitlement set and require a negative result.
negative_controls: Supply the two capabilities on different principals and reject the combination.
Supply non-overlapping resource scopes and reject the combination.
cleanup_and_restoration: Destroy the copied entitlement sets used for counterfactual checks.
Confirm no grant, role, or resource policy was altered.
blind_spots: Conditional denies may reduce an apparent effective entitlement.
Session constraints can narrow privileges after the snapshot was taken.

standards_mappings.rationale: Account manipulation provides context for harmful combinations of account grants.

techniques.name: Peer object identifier substitution
techniques.mechanic: Compare an owned-object fixture with a peer-object fixture under the same synthetic actor.
techniques.description: Detect an object-level decision that relies on identifier validity but omits ownership.
prerequisites: An offline decision trace contains one actor and two same-type synthetic objects.
Expected owner and policy decisions are declared for both objects.
observables: Actor, object, ownership, policy-rule, and decision identifiers.
Equivalent request shape with only the synthetic object identifier changed.
safe_proof: Replay the two stored decisions in a pure policy evaluator with no HTTP request.
Require allow for the owned fixture and deny for the peer fixture.
negative_controls: Use an unknown object identifier and require a deny outcome.
Use the peer owner as actor and require the expected allow outcome.
cleanup_and_restoration: Discard evaluator state after recording cited decision traces.
Verify fixture and policy digests remain unchanged.
blind_spots: A fixture cannot model undocumented application-side authorization hooks.
Opaque indirect identifiers may hide whether two objects share a type.

standards_mappings.rationale: Peer object substitution directly represents broken object-level authorization risk.

techniques.name: Nested subresource ownership mismatch
techniques.mechanic: Resolve parent and child ownership separately before evaluating a nested object route.
techniques.description: Detect a policy that validates a parent but fails to bind the requested child to that parent.
prerequisites: Synthetic parent-child records and ownership edges are complete for the fixture.
A stored route template identifies both parent and child selectors.
observables: Resolved parent owner, child owner, and parent-child relationship.
Policy trace showing which selector each authorization rule consumed.
safe_proof: Evaluate a mismatched child in an offline route-policy model.
Require the proof to stop at deny without invoking a resource handler.
negative_controls: Pair the parent with its legitimate child and require an allow decision.
Pair a legitimate child with an unauthorized parent and require a deny decision.
cleanup_and_restoration: Clear the in-memory route resolution table.
Reconcile parent-child fixture hashes against their baseline values.
blind_spots: Eventual consistency can make parent-child exports temporarily disagree.
Authorization performed downstream may be absent from a route-level trace.

standards_mappings.rationale: Nested resource ownership is a concrete object-level authorization boundary.

techniques.name: Bulk selector mixed-ownership decision
techniques.mechanic: Partition a synthetic bulk selector by per-object ownership before aggregate evaluation.
techniques.description: Find an aggregate authorization decision that masks one unauthorized object among owned ones.
prerequisites: A synthetic bulk request fixture contains at least two object identifiers.
Per-object ownership and expected all-or-nothing behavior are declared.
observables: The ordered object identifiers and their individual owner decisions.
Aggregate allow or deny decision with the governing policy rule.
safe_proof: Evaluate the stored selector without sending an API request.
Require a deny or explicit authorized subset when any object is unauthorized.
negative_controls: Use an all-owned selector and require its documented success behavior.
Use an all-peer selector and require a complete deny outcome.
cleanup_and_restoration: Erase the temporary selector partition after evidence capture.
Confirm object fixtures and ownership records are byte-identical to baseline.
blind_spots: Streaming endpoints may authorize objects after the initial aggregate decision.
Field-level filtering can obscure an object-level authorization defect.

standards_mappings.rationale: A mixed-ownership bulk selector exercises object-level authorization for every ID.

techniques.name: Writable service configuration path
techniques.mechanic: Join service start identity, configuration ACL, and binary ACL into a static privilege path.
techniques.description: Identify a synthetic service path where an unprivileged principal can alter privileged startup state.
prerequisites: Offline service configuration and ACL fixtures identify principals by stable SID aliases.
Privileged service identities and protected paths are labeled in the fixture.
observables: Service identity, start mode, configuration path, and binary path.
Effective write edges from the synthetic principal to service-controlled objects.
safe_proof: Construct a graph witness without editing a service or file.
Cite the exact access-control entries that complete the path.
negative_controls: Remove the write edge in a copied ACL and require no path.
Change the service identity to an unprivileged fixture and require no privileged endpoint.
cleanup_and_restoration: Delete copied ACL and service graph material after comparison.
Verify no service, registry key, or executable was created or modified.
blind_spots: Runtime security products can block changes allowed by a static ACL.
Service launch protections can invalidate a path inferred from configuration alone.

standards_mappings.rationale: Windows service configuration is the specific privilege-path surface modeled.

techniques.name: Privileged scheduled task edit path
techniques.mechanic: Connect task run identity to writable task definition and referenced action artifacts.
techniques.description: Model whether a synthetic user controls data consumed by a higher-privilege scheduled task.
prerequisites: Offline task definitions include run-as identity, triggers, and action paths.
ACL fixtures cover each task definition and referenced local artifact.
observables: Task run-as identity and action command metadata without executable content.
Write permission edges to the task definition or referenced artifact.
safe_proof: Emit a static task-to-artifact-to-principal path only.
Demonstrate path removal by tightening a copied ACL fixture.
negative_controls: Use a disabled task and require it to be classified non-triggerable.
Use a writable artifact referenced only by an unprivileged task and reject escalation.
cleanup_and_restoration: Dispose of copied task and ACL fixtures used by the proof.
Assert that task definitions, triggers, and files were never written.
blind_spots: A static task export may omit runtime credential restrictions.
Remote task actions can depend on permissions outside the endpoint fixture.

standards_mappings.rationale: Scheduled task metadata is the Windows task surface represented by this path.

techniques.name: Privileged startup artifact path
techniques.mechanic: Correlate startup location execution context with effective write access to its artifact.
techniques.description: Find a synthetic startup entry consumed by a more privileged logon context.
prerequisites: Startup entry fixtures state scope, consuming identity class, and artifact path.
Effective ACL fixtures are normalized for the unprivileged synthetic principal.
observables: Startup location and consuming identity class.
Artifact ownership plus inherited and explicit write permissions.
safe_proof: Report a read-only relationship path with no registry or filesystem write.
Prove dependency by removing the startup edge in an isolated graph copy.
negative_controls: Use a user-only startup entry and require no higher-privilege path.
Use a protected artifact ACL and require path rejection.
cleanup_and_restoration: Destroy the isolated relationship graph after the proof.
Compare registry and artifact fixture digests to their original values.
blind_spots: Application control policy can prevent execution despite the relationship.
Logon ordering can affect whether the startup artifact is consumed.

standards_mappings.rationale: Registry run keys and startup folders are the persistence surface being modeled.

techniques.name: Identity policy wildcard permission path
techniques.mechanic: Resolve principal-to-policy attachments and wildcard action-resource allows.
techniques.description: Trace a synthetic principal to an overbroad allow while preserving explicit deny precedence.
prerequisites: Normalized synthetic IAM policies include statements, attachments, and conditions.
The evaluation context supplies every condition key referenced by a statement.
observables: Principal, policy, statement, action, resource, and condition identifiers.
Matched explicit deny and allow statements in evaluation order.
safe_proof: Use a pure policy evaluator and emit only the decision trace.
Require an explicit deny to override a wildcard allow in the proof fixture.
negative_controls: Add a matching explicit deny and require the effective path to close.
Narrow the requested resource outside the allow scope and require denial.
cleanup_and_restoration: Clear the policy evaluation cache and synthetic request context.
Verify no policy version, attachment, or cloud object was changed.
blind_spots: Service-specific authorization rules may differ from the normalized evaluator.
Missing condition keys can make an offline decision indeterminate.

standards_mappings.rationale: Cloud account discovery is related context for the principals in an IAM path.

techniques.name: Cross-account role trust path
techniques.mechanic: Join caller permissions, role trust, and organization conditions across synthetic accounts.
techniques.description: Determine whether both sides of a modeled role assumption path are satisfied.
prerequisites: Caller policy, role trust policy, and organization metadata share stable account aliases.
External identifier and organization condition values are explicitly supplied or absent.
observables: Caller-side allow statement and target-side trust statement.
Condition results for organization, account, and external identifier constraints.
safe_proof: Evaluate the two policy halves without requesting any token.
Report the minimal cited statement set required for reachability.
negative_controls: Remove the caller-side allow and require the path to fail.
Use a nonmatching organization identifier and require the trust condition to fail.
cleanup_and_restoration: Delete the temporary cross-account adjacency index.
Confirm no role session, credential, or policy update was created.
blind_spots: Service control policies may block a path otherwise allowed by both role policies.
Federation session attributes may change condition evaluation.

standards_mappings.rationale: Additional cloud roles are related to cross-account role access paths.

techniques.name: Organization boundary effective permission path
techniques.mechanic: Intersect identity allow, permissions boundary, and organization policy layers.
techniques.description: Find a synthetic action that survives every applicable cloud IAM policy boundary.
prerequisites: The organization hierarchy and attached service control policies are immutable fixtures.
Identity policy and permissions boundary inputs use one normalized action vocabulary.
observables: Organization units traversed from account to root.
Allow or deny contribution from each policy layer for the action and resource.
safe_proof: Compute set intersection and deny precedence without a cloud control-plane call.
Cite every layer needed to support the final effective permission.
negative_controls: Attach a copied service control policy deny and require the path to close.
Remove the identity allow in a copied fixture and require no effective permission.
cleanup_and_restoration: Discard copied hierarchy and policy-layer fixtures.
Verify all original organization and IAM fixture hashes are unchanged.
blind_spots: Resource policies and session policies can add layers absent from this fixture.
Organization policy propagation delay is not represented offline.

standards_mappings.rationale: Cloud role discovery is related to resolving effective organization role paths.

techniques.name: Unauthorized inter-zone flow path
techniques.mechanic: Compare observed synthetic source-zone and destination-zone flows to the conduit matrix.
techniques.description: Detect a modeled flow that crosses an undeclared industrial zone boundary.
prerequisites: A synthetic zone inventory and approved conduit matrix have stable identifiers.
Offline flow records identify direction, protocol class, and observation time.
observables: Source zone, destination zone, conduit, and protocol class.
Policy matrix decision and cited flow record for each boundary crossing.
safe_proof: Compare immutable records only and emit no packet or rule change.
Report the matrix cell and flow identifier that demonstrate the mismatch.
negative_controls: Use a declared conduit flow and require a compliant result.
Reverse a one-way permitted flow and require an unauthorized result.
cleanup_and_restoration: Remove the derived zone-pair index after the comparison.
Verify the zone, conduit, and flow input digests remain unchanged.
blind_spots: Unmonitored serial or vendor links may not appear in flow records.
NAT can obscure the original industrial asset zone.

standards_mappings.rationale: Network segmentation aligns with checking traffic against defined zones and conduits.

techniques.name: Conduit boundary protection gap
techniques.mechanic: Join each declared conduit to its synthetic boundary enforcement and monitoring controls.
techniques.description: Identify a modeled conduit lacking a required deny, allowlist, or observation control.
prerequisites: Each conduit fixture names required control classes and enforcement points.
Boundary control inventory is a read-only synthetic configuration export.
observables: Conduit identifier, enforcement point, and configured control classes.
Required control class with present, absent, or indeterminate status.
safe_proof: Produce a configuration join result without connecting to industrial equipment.
Cite both the conduit requirement and control inventory records.
negative_controls: Provide a conduit with every required control and require no gap.
Provide an unreferenced control device and require it not to satisfy the conduit.
cleanup_and_restoration: Delete the temporary conduit-to-control join table.
Confirm no firewall, switch, gateway, or monitoring configuration changed.
blind_spots: A configuration export cannot show a failed enforcement process.
Proprietary gateway functions may not map cleanly to the control classes.

standards_mappings.rationale: Zone boundary protection aligns with verifying controls assigned to each conduit.

techniques.name: Temporary segmentation change restoration
techniques.mechanic: Compare pre-change, approved temporary, and restored synthetic rule-state snapshots.
techniques.description: Verify that a modeled maintenance conduit returns exactly to its recorded baseline.
prerequisites: Canonical before, temporary, and after rule snapshots share one device alias.
The approved temporary delta and restoration deadline are explicit fixture fields.
observables: Rules added, removed, or reordered in the temporary snapshot.
Residual differences between baseline and restored snapshots.
safe_proof: Apply the declared delta only to an in-memory model and compare canonical hashes.
Require the restored snapshot hash to equal the pre-change snapshot hash.
negative_controls: Leave one temporary rule in the restored fixture and require restoration failure.
Restore equivalent rules in a different order and evaluate documented order semantics.
cleanup_and_restoration: Erase the in-memory changed-state model after evidence generation.
Record failed-closed status for any residual and never assert live restoration.
blind_spots: Snapshot equality cannot confirm that a device loaded the configuration.
External controller state may reapply a temporary change after the snapshot.

standards_mappings.rationale: Control system recovery aligns with restoring and verifying a known configuration baseline.

limitations: This catalog describes offline synthetic evidence paths and grants no target authority.
A mapping supplies standards context but does not claim successful execution or impact.
Product, deployment, telemetry, and runtime behavior remain outside this reference catalog.
